description:
Port the Phase A coverage machinery (feature/q67-phase-a: Distributor singleton, placeholder materializer, on-demand recruitment, death healing, recovery relaxation, idle spin-down, warm re-adoption - q67.2-.7, .12, .13, cbj + tests) onto develop, ADAPTED to keyspace-mutation publication. PR #97 closed 2026-08-19; the branch is the audited reference implementation and is deleted once this lands.

WHAT CHANGES IN THE PORT (the FDB model, verified in ../foundationdb source):
- FDB's DD moves shards by transactionally mutating keyServers/ and serverKeys/ (MoveKeys.actor.cpp, krmSetRange); commit proxies observe those mutations AS THEY COMMIT and update their in-memory keyInfo range map (ApplyMetadataMutation.cpp:243-287); txnStateStore at the proxy holds the system metadata; clients ask proxies (GetKeyServerLocations) and invalidate on wrong_shard_server.
- Bedrock equivalents after bedrock-q67.20: the resolver->window->CommitProxy.Metadata pipeline IS ApplyMetadataMutation/txnStateStore; RoutingData in-batch application gives same-batch visibility. So the Distributor publishes coverage by COMMITTING ORDINARY TRANSACTIONS that mutate \xFF/system/materializer_keys/<end_key> (MaterializerList values; family + encoding already exist), and later shard_keys//shards/ for split/merge. Proxies learn routing with no new channel.
- DELETED from the phase-a version, not ported: Director.apply_tsl_delta, the tsl-delta hardening (bedrock-0u3 scope), and placeholder-into-TSL-slot swaps. Client read path (materializer lookup from proxy Metadata or metadata shard, invalidate-on-failure) is q67.9's design decision - this ticket lands the writer and the healing loop against whichever read path q67.9 picks.
- PersistencePhase note: once materializer_keys/ has a writer, its prefix joins the clear-before-rewrite set ONLY if recovery rewrites it (see bedrock-q67.20.3 survey) - decide ownership: recovery-written vs distributor-owned-only.

WHAT PORTS UNCHANGED IN SPIRIT: coverage sweep + demand channel ({:coverage_demand, tag}), bounded parking (min(client timeout, hold_ms), shed :unavailable), epoch-validated mutations (stale distributor self-terminates - now naturally enforced because its transactions carry its epoch), director re-recruits distributor on death, recovery stalls only for tag 0.

Sequencing: blocked by bedrock-q67.20 (pipeline must be on develop); blocks bedrock-q67.9's exit criterion (Distributor publishes via system keys; tsl_updated broadcast deleted) - land in coordination with q67.9. Same workflow as q67.20: TDD, stacked PRs, cold audit per layer.

comments.text: Audit 2026-08-20 (post trim campaign, stacks #161/#166 collapsed into feature/q67-phase-b-prereqs @ 3862a5b2): three references in this ticket are now stale. (1) 'family + encoding already exist' - no longer true: q67.31 deleted the MaterializerList codec and every unread system-key family under the 'a key without a reader is inventory, not communication' rule. materializer_keys/ returns WITH this ticket, writer and reader landing together, shaped by what the reader needs. (2) 'resolver->window->CommitProxy.Metadata pipeline' - CommitProxy.Metadata was deleted (q67.30); the pipeline's consumer is RoutingData (immutable gb_trees), applied under the serialized apply-then-route gate (q67.24). Window application is now the exact per-proxy relay (q67.33), fail-fast, converged-verdict (q67.22) - stronger than what this ticket assumed. (3) 'whichever read path q67.9 picks' - settled on q67.9 2026-08-20: FDB serves GetKeyServerLocations from proxies out of keyInfo; Bedrock's analogue is the proxy's RoutingData snapshot. This ticket lands the writer + healing loop against that. The PersistencePhase ownership question stands and should be answered by the q67.23 decision (seeded recover_from).

Deferred obligation from the 2026-08-20 side-channel campaign design: when the Distributor introduces mid-epoch materializer removal, retirement delivery goes IN-BAND, FDB-style - the proxy's apply-then-route step dual-routes a membership clear (materializers/<tag>) to the victim's own shard tag so the worker observes its own key cleared in the stream it already follows and self-retires (ApplyMetadataMutation.cpp privatization -> storageserver applyPrivateData worker_removed). Until then, retirement is recovery-boundary-only via foreman rejoin validation (course B). Do not build the private-mutation path before removals exist.

Obligation from the PR #182 audit (2026-08-20): the client-side LayoutIndex partial cache assumes shard-range disjointness, which holds today because recovery's per-epoch rewrite is the only boundary writer and invalidation is coarse. When the Distributor introduces mid-epoch boundary mutations, superseded ranges can coexist with their replacements in a live index with no invalidation trigger — the insert must become overlap-aware (or eviction per-range) BEFORE mid-epoch splits/moves land. Flagged in the LayoutIndex moduledoc.

title: Port Distributor + placeholder from phase-a: coverage published as keyspace mutations
